html:
The Sinhalese kingdom of ancient Sri Lanka, named after its capital city of Anuradhapura, which served as the island's capital for some 1,400 years. That makes it one of the longest-lived capitals in Asia.

Its early history comes from the Pali chronicles, above all the Mahavamsa, written centuries later. They say King Pandukabhaya founded the city in the 5th or 4th century BCE; the exact date is not certain.

The great turn came around 250 BCE, when Mahinda, a monk sent from Ashoka's India, converted King Devanampiya Tissa to Buddhism. A cutting of the tree under which the Buddha was awakened was planted in the city, and it still grows there. From then on the kings saw themselves as protectors of Buddhism, and the island became the home of the Theravada school. The Pali Canon was first written down in Sri Lanka in the 1st century BCE.

What the kingdom left:

  • Huge brick stupas, among the largest buildings of the ancient world, such as the Ruwanwelisaya and the Jetavanaramaya.
  • A system of great reservoirs, called tanks, and canals that fed rice fields across the dry zone of the island.
  • The fortress palace of Sigiriya, built by King Kashyapa in the late 5th century.

The island sat on sea routes between Rome, India and China, and its ports traded with all of them. Its kings fought often with invaders from south India, beginning with the Tamil kingdoms. In 993 the Chola Empire took the north, and by 1017 it held the whole island. When Sinhalese rule returned, the capital moved to Polonnaruwa.
sum: The Sinhalese kingdom of ancient Sri Lanka, named after its capital city of Anuradhapura, which served as the island's capital for some 1,400 years. That makes it one of the longest-lived capitals in Asia.
